title: Never signed, still bound by the award?

scenes.dialogue: A government never signs a contract, but joins the whole arbitration without protest. Once the award comes, can it refuse to pay, saying it was never a party?
Here, the tipping fee alone was raised to over twenty five crore rupees. Yet the award holder could go after just one municipality's property. Was that right?

scenes.dialogue: Nobody on the paying side challenged it, so it became final. In execution, the government said it never signed the contract, so its assets were off limits.
The executing court rejected that, but held government departments' property could not be attached, since the contracts covered only the municipalities.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? Having taken part without protest, and never challenged the award, the government could not deny being a party.
All four judgment debtors were jointly and severally liable, so the limit was set aside. If they do not settle in eight weeks, execution can go against them all.
